preparedFrom: BBM Scraper Operating Manual (the course deck under docs/courses/bbm-scraper-manual)
notes: These questions and answers were authored from the BBM Scraper manual content to seed the IN-DECK graded assessment (Option B). Every answer here is verified:false — the training authority (Ash Wyborn) must review and confirm each one before this is used to certify anyone.
Marking is exact-set-match: the candidate must select every listed answer and nothing else.

IN-DECK MODEL: unlike track-dozer.answer-key.json (which pairs answers to an imported PDF's fields IN ORDER), each question here carries an explicit `fieldId`. That SAME id is used by the deck's graded card (data-field-id) and MUST be the id of the matching keyed question on the assessment tool's template version, so POST /answer grades the deck's selection against this key and the ✓/✗ lands on the tool's outcomeTarget. Reconcile these ids with the imported 'Authorised to Operate Scraper' template (or author the tool's theory fields with these ids) before go-live.

SENSITIVE: this file is an answer key to a safety-critical assessment. Repository read access is answer access. The API strips answerKey from every fill-surface payload (stripMarkingSecrets); this source file's audience is authoring staff only.
`answer` uses the deck option `val`s (mc: a/b/c/…, tf: true/false). The tool's answerKey uses the matching option VALUES on the real field.

questions.question: You may operate the scraper if you feel confident, even without a current Authority to Operate.
questions.note: False — no person operates any SME unless authorised, holds a current Authority to Operate, and is deemed competent; if not, stop and speak to the Supervisor (Module A, Authorised Use of SME).

questions.question: What must you do before starting a scraper task?

options.text: Start work and assess hazards as you go
Locate the work area and complete a basic risk assessment
Wait for the Supervisor to complete the risk assessment for you

questions.note: Operator accountabilities: locate the work area and complete a basic risk assessment before starting (Module A).

questions.question: Access to a scraper work area by anyone other than the area WAPL or Contractor Supervisor is granted…

options.text: at any time, provided they wear hi-vis
only once all scrapers in the area have stopped

questions.note: Access is granted only once all scrapers have stopped; work resumes when the vehicle has left and the area is clear (Module A, Supervision, Signage & Access).

questions.question: What is the minimum standing travel separation between scrapers on the circuit?
questions.note: 40 m is the minimum travel distance / standing separation on the circuit (Module B, Travel Distance & Separation).

questions.question: In a loading, stripping or stockpile-reclaim zone, the minimum separation reduces to…

options.text: no minimum applies in a loading zone

questions.note: 20 m in a loading zone / stripping area / reclaiming a stockpile (Module B).

questions.question: It is acceptable to cut a cross-slope track with a scraper if no other machine is available.
questions.note: False — never cut a cross-slope track with a scraper; use a track machine or grader (Module B, Haul Route Preparation).

questions.question: In push-pull operations, how many scrapers may couple together at one time?

options.text: As many as the cut will hold

questions.note: Only two scrapers couple at one time — trains of three or more are not authorised (Module C, Push-Pull Operations).

questions.question: You may load the bowl before the cushion hitch is locked down, as long as you do it gently.
questions.note: False — never load the bowl unless the cushion hitch is locked down (Module C, Dozer-Assisted & Self-Loading).

questions.question: What is the minimum clearance from a vertical mining face when designing a stockpile?
questions.note: 5 m minimum clearance from a vertical mining face (Module D, Stockpile Design).

questions.question: When reclaiming a stockpile, what is the minimum distance you must stay from any stockpile edge?
questions.note: Stay a minimum of 1 m from any stockpile edge; approach the cut straight on and reclaim in straight sections only (Module D, Reclaiming Stockpiles).

questions.question: Rock and tree roots may be dumped on the stockpile edge to build it out.
questions.note: False — never dump rock or tree roots on the edge; a cutting edge catching them slides the rear wheels off. Dump in the middle or remove to the side (Module D, Building Stockpiles).

questions.question: If your scraper becomes bogged or bellied out, you should attempt to retrieve it yourself if the situation looks minor.
questions.note: False — do not attempt to retrieve a bogged/bellied scraper; it can make things worse. A JHA must be completed before any removal (Module E, incident response).

questions.question: After an incident in the work area, what must you do?

options.text: Keep working and report it at the end of shift
Stop work immediately, call the area Supervisor, and ensure evidence is gathered
Move the machine clear before anyone arrives

questions.note: Stop work immediately, call the area Supervisor for assistance, and evidence must be gathered (Module E, incident response).

questions.question: On steep slopes you should always travel straight up or straight down, never across.
questions.note: True — always travel straight up or straight down steep slopes (Module E, rehabilitation / putting the ground back).
